failure_class: Unchecked call and return types
root_invariant: Every callable use satisfies its resolved parameter and result relation
proposed_treatment: Finish instantiate/infer/unify and return checking before claiming downstream soundness

failure_class: Representation mistaken for nominal identity
root_invariant: ABI equivalence never implies domain-type equivalence
proposed_treatment: Keep nominal identity through checking; erase only during certified lowering

failure_class: Unknown evidence treated as harmless
root_invariant: Unresolved facts are Blocked, not pure, public or universally placeable
proposed_treatment: No successful contract or code generation may depend on unresolved semantic facts

failure_class: Generic arguments or binders lost
root_invariant: Type arguments and binder identity participate in every relevant relation
proposed_treatment: Decide callable-generic surface; recursively resolve and substitute once

failure_class: Absence confused with valid data
root_invariant: Absent, unknown, empty and default have distinct meanings where the domain distinguishes them
proposed_treatment: Derive explicit presence decoding; preserve domain-specific default policy

failure_class: Impossible state combinations and ignored variants
root_invariant: Represent alternatives as variants and handle every reachable alternative
proposed_treatment: Derive exhaustive matches from resolved constructors; separately validate runtime transitions

failure_class: Quantity and identifier conflation
root_invariant: Meaningful units and identifier domains cannot be silently interchanged
proposed_treatment: Standard quantity/identifier types; conversions name policy and possible loss

failure_class: Arithmetic precision, overflow and rounding loss
root_invariant: Numeric operations preserve their declared range and rounding semantics or fail explicitly
proposed_treatment: Checked size/time arithmetic; money rounding policy; lossless wire codecs

failure_class: Structural validity mistaken for authoritative truth
root_invariant: Decoding establishes shape, not the authority of the fact
proposed_treatment: Separate untrusted input, validated shape and server-endorsed domain evidence

failure_class: A valid transition violates an aggregate business invariant
root_invariant: Reachable distributed states must preserve declared business constraints
proposed_treatment: Name aggregate invariants and coordination owner; do not infer business rules from types alone

failure_class: Polymorphic generalization shares incompatible mutable state
root_invariant: A generalized value cannot share mutable storage across incompatible instantiations
proposed_treatment: Define generalization with mutation/effect inference; test mutable closures and valid pure higher-order functions

failure_class: Variance widens a mutable or capability-bearing value unsafely
root_invariant: Substitution preserves both permitted writes and accepted inputs
proposed_treatment: Infer variance from definitions; keep authority-bearing mutable parameters invariant where required

failure_class: Handled capability requirement is mistaken for observational purity
root_invariant: Discharging an effect interface does not prove that execution has no externally observable consequence
proposed_treatment: State distinct judgments for purity, needed authority, captured authority and placement; do not infer one by erasing another

failure_class: Multi-shot resumption duplicates affine resources or business effects
root_invariant: Continuation reuse respects captured resource multiplicity and observable effect semantics
proposed_treatment: Keep ordinary platform effects one-shot; require proof or confined pure region for multi-shot reuse

failure_class: Foreign exception, trap or cancellation bypasses declared failure handling
root_invariant: Failure across an adapter boundary is represented or terminates its explicit isolation domain
proposed_treatment: Map recoverable foreign failures; distinguish cancellation, domain rejection and fatal host fault

failure_class: Type inference or verification itself becomes unbounded work
root_invariant: Interactive checking has bounded resource use and explicit unsupported/timeout results
proposed_treatment: Bound recursive inference/solver expansion; cache sound summaries; expose unknown rather than accepting as proven

failure_class: Route-only authorization bypass
root_invariant: Every protected operation enforces authorization independently of the route taken
proposed_treatment: Derive checks at commands/queries and enforce on every entry, including direct RPC

failure_class: Object or tenant confused after authentication
root_invariant: An authenticated subject is authorized for this object, action and tenant
proposed_treatment: Bind resource identity to tenant/principal evidence and check dynamic equality at use

failure_class: Revoked rights remain usable through cached authority
root_invariant: Authority used for an operation meets its required policy revision
proposed_treatment: Define authorization freshness, revocation propagation and fail-closed behavior

failure_class: Check/use race on changing protected state
root_invariant: Authorization predicates and protected mutation refer to a coherent state
proposed_treatment: Check within transaction or validate a revision-bound precondition at commit

failure_class: Confused deputy and authority laundering
root_invariant: A callee may use only authority intentionally delegated for this action
proposed_treatment: No ambient escalation through helpers, callbacks, jobs or adapters; preserve caller and purpose

failure_class: Delegation accidentally broadens authority
root_invariant: Delegation cannot increase resource, action, time or audience scope
proposed_treatment: Support attenuation and expiry in standard capability adapters; validate at runtime

failure_class: Privileged support action lacks accountable identity
root_invariant: Effective subject and initiating actor remain distinct for sensitive actions
proposed_treatment: Carry actor, subject and delegated purpose in command context and audit records

failure_class: Process or placement grant mistaken for operation authority
root_invariant: Linking an allowed component does not authorize every operation or object
proposed_treatment: Keep import identity, ABI shape, capability set and runtime object policy separate

failure_class: Private data enters a shared materialization
root_invariant: A public artifact cannot depend on session/device/secret data without authorized release
proposed_treatment: Propagate labels through values and control flow; enforce actual runtime audience

failure_class: Implicit or derived leak bypasses direct field checks
root_invariant: Branches, errors, aggregates and identifiers can carry restricted information
proposed_treatment: Specify supported noninterference model, including error/control dependencies

failure_class: Secret captured in client code or transport metadata
root_invariant: Code, manifests, captures, source maps and diagnostics are data sinks too
proposed_treatment: Run release-artifact privacy scans over emitted outputs, not just ordinary serializers

failure_class: Telemetry bypasses application privacy rules
root_invariant: Telemetry collection obeys the same audience and purpose constraints as application output
proposed_treatment: Typed logging and tracing sinks with default minimization and bounded redaction

failure_class: Declassification authorized by attacker-controlled conditions
root_invariant: The release decision itself must have appropriate integrity and authority
proposed_treatment: Separate endorsement from release; audit both the decision and released projection

failure_class: Sensitive history or offline snapshots survive logout
root_invariant: Retained browser representations obey their own confidentiality and retention policy
proposed_treatment: Classify history, bfcache, IDB and offline drafts; purge owned stores on identity change

failure_class: Deletion removes primary row but not derived copies
root_invariant: Deletion has an explicit closure over owned derived representations
proposed_treatment: Model erasure requests, derived-copy inventory, tombstones and completion evidence

failure_class: Purpose or consent changes do not reach ongoing collection
root_invariant: Use authorization is scoped by purpose and can change during a session
proposed_treatment: Gate collection at use, propagate policy epochs and stop ongoing owned collectors

failure_class: Placement satisfies secrecy but violates data residency
root_invariant: Processing and storage locations satisfy independently declared residency constraints
proposed_treatment: Propagate residency to caches, replicas, telemetry, backups and vendor adapters

failure_class: In-process IFC mistaken for complete side-channel protection
root_invariant: A guarantee must state which observations and adversaries it excludes
proposed_treatment: State timing, shared hardware, malicious browser and out-of-band limits; offer isolation tiers

failure_class: Text becomes executable markup or code
root_invariant: Untrusted text cannot enter an executable sink through ordinary interpolation
proposed_treatment: Context-sensitive HTML/attribute/URL/CSS output; no universal SafeString

failure_class: Sanitized HTML is reused in an incompatible or mutated context
root_invariant: A sanitization proof applies only to its policy, context and unchanged result
proposed_treatment: Opaque sanitized fragment type; invalidation on mutation; versioned sanitizer boundary

failure_class: URL or redirect authority confused with string escaping
root_invariant: A syntactically encoded URL is not permission to navigate, fetch or load it
proposed_treatment: Distinct navigation, media and server-fetch URL policies; validate schemes and redirect targets

failure_class: Data concatenated into SQL or shell syntax
root_invariant: Values cannot acquire interpreter syntax authority
proposed_treatment: Generate bound parameters; identifiers and executable names require separate capabilities

failure_class: SSRF restriction bypassed by resolution or redirects
root_invariant: Every actual network destination remains within the granted egress scope
proposed_treatment: Validate resolution and each redirect; enforce network policy below application code

failure_class: Deserializer reconstructs behavior instead of data
root_invariant: External payloads cannot select arbitrary executable behavior or privileged references
proposed_treatment: Decode bounded data-only schemas; separately authenticate permitted operation identity

failure_class: Object property input mutates prototypes or ambient names
root_invariant: Untrusted keys cannot alter language/runtime lookup authority
proposed_treatment: Copy decoded records into inert structures; restrict path setters and prototype access

failure_class: Uploaded content executes or exhausts processing resources
root_invariant: Upload acceptance does not imply trusted name, media type, content or processing cost
proposed_treatment: Typed upload lifecycle: received, validated, scanned, published; enforce quotas and decompression bounds

failure_class: Browser protections are inconsistent with generated content
root_invariant: Generated CSP/Trusted Types policies admit required code without silently broadening trust
proposed_treatment: Derive hashes/nonces and sink policy; test unsupported targets with safe generated behavior

failure_class: Oversized or adversarial valid input consumes unbounded work
root_invariant: Type validity does not imply bounded parsing, validation or execution cost
proposed_treatment: Bound bytes, depth, expansion and work; select safe regex implementation; reject unsupported costly constructs where knowable

failure_class: Session fixation or wrong renewal semantics
root_invariant: Privilege changes cannot reuse attacker-chosen session authority
proposed_treatment: Generate session establishment, rotation, expiry and revocation lifecycle

failure_class: Account switching retains old principal-bound state
root_invariant: All private work and retained state are scoped to a concrete identity epoch
proposed_treatment: Advance identity epoch, detach old work and refuse stale private completions

failure_class: Authenticated browser request lacks intentional authorization
root_invariant: Ambient credentials do not prove that this origin/user intended the action
proposed_treatment: Generate request-intent defenses for each supported transport and non-JS form path

failure_class: CORS confused with access control
root_invariant: Read permission in a browser is distinct from server operation authorization
proposed_treatment: Keep origin allowlists separate from command authority; reject credentialed wildcard policy

failure_class: Cookie scope exposes session authority unnecessarily
root_invariant: Cookie lifetime, domain, path and transport match the session's intended scope
proposed_treatment: Generate constrained cookies and integration-specific exceptions; audit subdomain trust

failure_class: OAuth callback belongs to another issuer or interaction
root_invariant: Callback issuer, client, redirect and initiating interaction must match
proposed_treatment: Provider adapter owns state/nonce/issuer/redirect validation and token-audience checks

failure_class: Untrusted callback replay repeats a protected action
root_invariant: Authenticated message authenticity is distinct from freshness and duplicate suppression
proposed_treatment: Verify raw bytes then bind sender/account/event identity; reject expired replay where contract permits

failure_class: Cross-origin embedding grants more browser authority than intended
root_invariant: Framing, permission delegation and operation authority are separate grants
proposed_treatment: Generate frame and permissions policies; review origin isolation against legitimate embeds

failure_class: Imperative resource outlives its owner
root_invariant: Every owned resource has one lifetime and a release path
proposed_treatment: Infer owners; generated cleanup on success, failure, cancellation and replacement

failure_class: Scope cancellation merely changes bookkeeping
root_invariant: Cancellation has defined adapter semantics, not just a cancellation counter
proposed_treatment: Propagate cancellation to cancellable work; separately fence late results from uncancellable work

failure_class: Completed stale work publishes after owner loss
root_invariant: A completion may publish only for the still-current owner/request generation
proposed_treatment: Compare generation/identity epoch before cache or UI publication

failure_class: Deduplicated consumer receives no shared result
root_invariant: Deduplication shares the result or failure, not only execution count
proposed_treatment: One request state machine per key; every admitted subscriber observes the same terminal outcome

failure_class: One consumer cancels work still needed by another
root_invariant: Work lifetime follows aggregate live demand, subject to explicit ownership policy
proposed_treatment: Track live subscribers; release underlying work only after final demand or deadline

failure_class: Declared timeout is not enforced
root_invariant: Deadline policy must affect running work and result publication
proposed_treatment: Use actual deadlines across queueing, connection, execution and retries; adapter-specific enforcement

failure_class: Detached task accidentally loses authority or durability
root_invariant: Escaping a scope requires explicit durable or detached authority and retained context
proposed_treatment: Distinguish request child, supervised service task and durable workflow

failure_class: Resource released twice or used after transfer
root_invariant: Ownership transfer invalidates the old use path
proposed_treatment: Affine API handles; generated lifetime guards for foreign/runtime calls

failure_class: Cleanup itself fails or blocks indefinitely
root_invariant: Cleanup has bounded behavior and preserves primary failure information
proposed_treatment: Bound asynchronous release; collect suppressed cleanup failures; isolate poisoned handles

failure_class: Hidden listeners, observers or object URLs retain resources
root_invariant: Every retained callback or native allocation is attributed to a live owner
proposed_treatment: Generate disposal for observers/listeners/timers/object URLs/workers and instrument retained ownership

failure_class: Read-modify-write loses a concurrent update
root_invariant: A transition's assumptions must still hold when its write commits
proposed_treatment: Compile declared preconditions into atomic checks at the authoritative store

failure_class: Individually valid writes violate a cross-row invariant
root_invariant: Transactions must preserve the declared aggregate invariant under permitted concurrency
proposed_treatment: Select sufficient enforcement for known transactions; reject unsupported guarantees instead of promising generic snapshot safety

failure_class: Reactive consumers observe an impossible intermediate combination
root_invariant: A declared local transaction publishes a stabilized, coherent observation
proposed_treatment: Define transaction boundaries and scheduling semantics for derived graphs

failure_class: Optimistic rollback erases a later successful edit
root_invariant: Rejecting one intent must remove only that intent's contribution
proposed_treatment: Maintain confirmed base plus pending pure transitions; rebase or serialize noncommuting operations

failure_class: Notification of new state is mistaken for applied state
root_invariant: Known remote version and locally realized version are distinct facts
proposed_treatment: Retain existing separate version semantics and adversarial ordering corpus

failure_class: Incidental object identity controls remote request lifetime
root_invariant: Logical resource identity, not allocation or rendering, determines query identity
proposed_treatment: Preserve semantic keys and demand ownership; complete result-sharing proof F04

failure_class: Rendering or derivation secretly performs an external action
root_invariant: Reading a description must not initiate externally observable work
proposed_treatment: Check effects transitively through higher-order calls and resolved foreign boundaries

failure_class: Reactive dependency changes leave obsolete edges or cycles
root_invariant: Dynamic dependency membership changes atomically and converges under the declared cycle policy
proposed_treatment: Remove obsolete edges; diagnose static cycles; bound or explicitly model feedback

failure_class: Priority scheduling changes observable application meaning
root_invariant: Scheduling may reorder work only within the program's observation and causality contract
proposed_treatment: Separate priority hints from semantic order; test priority permutations

failure_class: Concurrent duplicate commands both execute
root_invariant: Claiming an operation and recording its effect must enforce one admissible execution
proposed_treatment: Atomic claim plus effect/result persistence where supported; external effects require provider protocol

failure_class: Same idempotency key names different operations or payloads
root_invariant: Idempotency binds tenant, operation version and canonical intent, not an arbitrary string alone
proposed_treatment: Reject conflicting reuse; do not deduplicate deliberate separate interactions

failure_class: Lost response is reported as definite failure
root_invariant: Transport failure cannot establish whether an irreversible effect committed
proposed_treatment: Expose pending, committed, rejected and unknown; reconcile without inventing a new intent

failure_class: Idempotency guarantee silently expires before replay does
root_invariant: Replay horizon cannot exceed the guaranteed deduplication horizon without an explicit outcome
proposed_treatment: Relate offline queues, webhook retries and dedup retention; reject incompatible guarantees

failure_class: State commits but its notification is lost
root_invariant: State change and publication intent are atomic at the authoritative transaction boundary
proposed_treatment: Keep existing outbox; test crash after commit and before acknowledgement across restarts

failure_class: Event is duplicated, reordered or skipped on reconnect
root_invariant: Consumers distinguish duplicate, next, gap and superseded events
proposed_treatment: Generate deduplication and gap detection; resnapshot when replay unavailable

failure_class: Compensation is treated as reversing history
root_invariant: Compensation is another fallible domain action, not time reversal
proposed_treatment: Represent compensation pending, failed and manual resolution; never infer arbitrary inverse

failure_class: Durable workflow replay uses changed nondeterministic behavior
root_invariant: Replayed history must produce compatible workflow decisions
proposed_treatment: Record nondeterministic inputs and version decisions; keep incompatible code isolated or migrate explicitly

failure_class: Cancellation is mistaken for undoing a committed effect
root_invariant: Stopping interest and stopping an uncommitted action are distinct from reversing a commit
proposed_treatment: Separate cancel request, cancelled-before-commit and already-committed outcomes
